absent: Semantics of shared page-table walk core, user-table conversion, initial table layout, non-execute mask and isolation feature test.
Address-marker array layout, index enumeration values and numeric base addresses for direct map, allocation, memory-model, descriptor, sanitizer, high-memory, fixed-map and entry areas.
Exception-table search implementation, control-word mask positions and numeric values for handler-type selectors and flag bits.
Register offset helper, full register-state layout beyond touched fields, instruction decode and operand helpers, and enclave marker value.
Flexible-event helpers, extended selector and event-data layouts, error-code propagation rules and return-instruction semantics.
Legacy firmware recovery addresses, packet-filter handler, machine-check control-register helper, bug handler and paravirtual checks.
Early recursion counter, early console and halt primitives, code-segment constant and trap-number values.
Tracing probe and fault-page structures, address-lookup levels, page-mask helpers, disarm and arm operations and step-completion release.
Linear-address conversion, mode predicates, fault-disable scope, safe-fetch failure modes and user-copy helpers.
Allocation range bounds, task-size limit, middle-size constants, top-level list and descriptor layouts and per-space lock placement.
Page-table accessor semantics, presence and leaf predicates, backing queries, control-register readers and high-memory threshold value.
Trace-event definitions, configuration defaults and logging helper implementations.

findings.text: Two write-execute verification services are provided. The user-table service has no result and stays silent when non-execute or isolation support is missing, otherwise it walks the user copy of the initial top level with verification enabled. The kernel-table service yields a boolean verdict, succeeding vacuously without non-execute support and otherwise walking the initial table with verification enabled.

Boot-time initializer populating dump-marker start addresses that are not fixed at build time. Sixty-four-bit builds cover direct map, allocation area start and memory-model start plus optional local-descriptor and sanitizer ranges. Thirty-two-bit builds cover allocation bounds, fixed-map start and entry area plus optional high-memory and local-descriptor ranges. Always reports success.

Fixup destinations are self-relative displacements resolved from their own storage location. Default handling optionally clears general result slots according to flag bits in the entry, then redirects the saved instruction location to the resolved destination and reports the event handled.

Exception entries observed here combine a self-relative fixup displacement with a packed control word. The control word carries a handler-type selector, a register selector and a signed immediate, plus independent flags requesting clearing of result slots. Absence of an entry is distinct from a present entry selecting the none type.

Numeric register selection is validated through an offset helper. Invalid selectors produce a one-time warning and resolve to a stable dummy cell rather than an invalid address, so callers may safely store through the returned pointer.

Word-tail synthesis for faulting loads succeeds only under a narrow conjunction of properties involving bounded distance to the fixup, successful decode with exact length agreement, expected load shape and width, resolvable reference whose aligned base relation matches the fault address, and resolvable destination. Success materializes the partial word with shift by trailing offset and then applies default redirection, while any mismatch reports unhandled.

Two trap-reporting fixups preserve trap identity in the primary result slot before default redirection. The plain form records the trap number alone while the SGX form records the trap number combined with a dedicated enclave-exit marker.

The floating-point restore fixup signals invalid processor extended state with a one-time warning identifying the faulting location, invokes the dedicated reset helper, and then applies default redirection.

User-access fault handling includes a plausibility test for protection faults on sixty-four-bit builds, accepting user-canonical addresses and the page immediately above that range. Implausible protection faults emit a one-time warning about non-canonical access before default redirection.

Control-register access failures distinguish read versus write and checked versus unchecked forms. Unchecked failures produce rate-limited diagnostics identifying direction, target selector and faulting location with a register dump. Failed reads are emulated as zero. Checked forms additionally record an input-output error in the selected register. All forms complete with default redirection.

Three compact fixups share default completion. The segment form reloads the FS selector with an ordered workaround when a null-selector processor bug is enabled. The immediate form places the encoded immediate into the selected register. The copy-length form derives remaining count from scaled base plus selected register content into the count slot and then applies user-access handling.

Flexible return-to-user fault handling converges the faulting user frame and the handler frame. On success the handler frame carries the blocked-interrupt indication for prompt release, event data and extended selector state are synchronized to the user frame, architectural code and stack selectors are preserved, moved and level state is cleared in the restored frame, and the error value is recorded in the saved origin slot before default redirection. Correctness depends on non-overlap of successive flexible frames due to reservation plus alignment.

Central fixup lookup and dispatch are exported. Type query by instruction address yields none when no entry exists. Main dispatch by saved instruction location extracts type, register and immediate selectors and routes among default, fault, access, segment, floating-point, packet-filter, register, length, padding, enclave, control-register and flexible-return families, with stack adjustment for pop-into-register and fatal termination for unrecognized or machine-check control paths.

Dispatch moves from table search to at most one typed handler. Missing entries report unhandled without side effects. Present entries commit to the selected family and normally return its verdict. Machine-check control-register paths and unknown selectors terminate fatally rather than returning. A legacy firmware recovery diversion precedes table lookup when enabled.

Early boot trap entry provides restricted handling before full initialization. Non-maskable interrupts are ignored, repeated recursion diverts to infinite halt, non-kernel code selectors are rejected except on paravirtual Xen, full dispatch is attempted with the saved error value, undefined-opcode faults consult the bug handler, and all remaining failures emit panic diagnostics with vector and processor state before halting.

Several failure modes do not return. Unknown fixup selectors and machine-check control paths reach a fatal trap. Early handling halts after recursion, selector rejection, unhandled faults or unresolved undefined opcodes. Floating-point repair warns of invalid state, so consumers must assume prior extended state is discarded.

Kernel memory-mapped IO fault handling is exported for page-fault integration. Distinct outcomes separate invalid address lookup, absence of tracing state, busy per-CPU context, and successful arming for single-step, letting callers decide whether normal fault processing should continue.

The fault-site gate consults memory-mapped IO tracing only while that facility is active. Claimed faults are signaled with a negative status and all other situations report zero, preserving the normal fault path when tracing is idle or uninterested.

Per-CPU tracing allows at most one in-flight fault. From idle it captures fault page and probe, preserves single-step and interrupt flag state, optionally notifies a pre-handler, arms single-step with interrupts masked, and makes the page present for stepping. An additional fault targeting the identical page while busy is left for normal not-present processing, while a fault on another page while busy is disarmed with emergency logging. Release of the busy state belongs to the step-completion path outside these fragments.

Tracing holds a non-tracing scheduler read-side critical section across probe lookup and step arming. The section suppresses preemption and migration so the per-CPU context remains stable through arming, with explicit release on every path that does not arm stepping while the armed path retains protection across the step.

Prefetch filtering is confined to a narrow legacy vendor, family and model envelope with build gating. Instruction-fetch faults are never filtered. Otherwise a single maximum-length window from the converted linear address is examined with faults disabled, using mode-appropriate safe fetch, and only specific prefix sequences and two-byte prefetch shapes confirm filtering.

Kernel mapping synchronization nests a global page-table spin lock outside a per-address-space table lock. The global lock protects iteration over the shared top-level list while the inner lock protects each individual propagation step for paravirtual needs. Single-address propagation itself assumes the caller holds the appropriate synchronization.

Single-address synchronization propagates only at the middle level from the reference table. Missing reference coverage at upper or middle stages reports absence without modification. Divergent presence triggers adoption of the reference middle value, absent reference middle reports absence, and otherwise backing equality is asserted before returning the reference middle entry.

Allocation-area fault handling validates range membership, derives the current top level from the control register instead of task state for interrupt safety, synchronizes the single address, accepts large-leaf coverage immediately, and otherwise requires a present leaf entry, reporting failure in all other cases.

Range synchronization entry iterates at middle granularity but acts only on the kernel portion below the allocation-area end, applying single-address propagation to every tracked top level under the documented nested locking.

Diagnostic page-table dump walks the current hierarchy for one address from the control register and reports middle and leaf values with width-scaled output. The walk stops before leaf access when backing is high, absent or a large leaf, avoiding direct access to high-memory tables. Segmented builds add a top-level prefix line through alternate logging aliases.

Processor state touched here spans general result and count slots, saved instruction and stack locations, flag state with single-step and interrupt bits, code and stack selectors with extended flexible views, saved origin or error slot, and event data. Handlers consume fault location and error values and produce redirection targets, emulated results and flag updates in place.

Remaining hazards include fatal backing mismatch during middle-level adoption, unexpected secondary tracing hits suggesting lost presence state, recursive tracing faults on another page while busy, cross-CPU accesses during stepping that succeed without events, and implausible user-access protection faults that only warn before handling.
Presence of the trace-creation macro in the fault translation unit is the stable build contract that instantiates fault trace events for this compilation.

Stable facts include a dedicated BIOS erratum warning for a legacy K8 issue, a fifteen-byte maximum window for prefetch inspection, and maximum-size plus width and alignment rules governing word-tail synthesis.
